title: Proverbs Chapter 30 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 30 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 30 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 30.

questions.question: In Proverbs 30, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Every word of God is pure
There is a generation that curseth
questions.correctAnswer: The words of Agur
questions.explanation: The first verse introduces Agur and his prophecy, as stated in Proverbs 30:1.

questions.question: Who is the author of the words in Proverbs 30?
questions.correctAnswer: Agur
questions.explanation: Agur is identified as the author in Proverbs 30:1.

questions.question: What does Agur claim about his understanding in Proverbs 30?
options: I am more brutish than any man
questions.correctAnswer: I am more brutish than any man
questions.explanation: Agur states his lack of understanding in Proverbs 30:2.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 30:3, what does Agur claim about his knowledge?
options: I have the knowledge of the holy
I am wise in my own eyes
questions.correctAnswer: I neither learned wisdom
questions.explanation: Agur clearly states in Proverbs 30:3 that he has not learned wisdom.

questions.question: What question is posed about who has ascended to heaven in Proverbs 30?
options: Who hath established all the ends of the earth?
Who hath ascended up into heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Who hath ascended up into heaven?
questions.explanation: This question is explicitly mentioned in Proverbs 30:4.

questions.question: What is said about the words of God in Proverbs 30:5?
questions.correctAnswer: They are pure
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:5 states that every word of God is pure.

questions.question: What warning is given in Proverbs 30:6?
options: Do not add to His words
questions.correctAnswer: Do not add to His words
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:6 warns against adding to God's words.

questions.question: What two things does Agur request in Proverbs 30:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Two things have I required
questions.explanation: Agur states in Proverbs 30:7 that he has two requests he wants before he dies.

questions.question: What does Agur ask to be removed from him in Proverbs 30:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Vanity and lies
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:8 mentions Agur's request to remove vanity and lies from him.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 30:9, what might happen if Agur is full?
options: He will know the name of God
questions.correctAnswer: He will deny the Lord
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:9 states that if he is full, he might deny God.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:10 advise regarding servants?
options: Accuse not a servant unto his master
questions.correctAnswer: Accuse not a servant unto his master
questions.explanation: This instruction is found in Proverbs 30:10.

questions.question: Does Proverbs 30 mention a generation that curses their father?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:11 mentions a generation that curseth their father.

questions.question: Is it stated in Proverbs 30 that Agur asked for wisdom?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:7 shows that Agur had requests, but he does not specifically ask for wisdom.

questions.question: Proverbs 30 states that Agur is a king.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not state that Agur is a king; it identifies him as the son of Jakeh.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 30, all words of God are impure.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:5 states that every word of God is pure, not impure.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 30 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 30 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:12 say about a certain generation?
options: They are pure in their own eyes
They are wise beyond their years
questions.correctAnswer: They are pure in their own eyes
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:12 states that there is a generation that believes they are pure in their own eyes but are not cleansed from their moral filth.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:13 warn about the generation with lofty eyes?
options: They will be admired by all
questions.correctAnswer: They will be brought low
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:13 indicates that the generation described as having lofty eyes may face consequences for their pride, implying a downward trajectory.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Proverbs 30:14 to describe a generation that devours the needy?
questions.correctAnswer: Their teeth are as swords
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:14 uses the imagery of teeth as swords to illustrate the violent and predatory nature of this generation towards the poor.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:15 say about things that are never satisfied?
options: They are only found in nature
They are represented by three things
They are represented by four things
questions.correctAnswer: They are represented by four things
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:15 mentions three things that are never satisfied and concludes with a fourth, emphasizing their insatiable nature.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 30:16, which of the following is NOT listed as something that is never satisfied?
options: The earth that is not filled with water
questions.correctAnswer: A hungry man
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:16 lists specific entities that are never satisfied, and a hungry man is not included in this list.

questions.question: What consequence does Proverbs 30:17 describe for the eye that mocks its father?
questions.correctAnswer: It will be punished
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:17 warns that the eye that mocks its father will face dire consequences, illustrated by the ravens picking it out.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:18 identify as too wonderful for the speaker?
options: The way of a wise man
The way of an eagle in the air
The way of a rich man
questions.correctAnswer: The way of an eagle in the air
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:19 lists the way of an eagle in the air among other mysteries that are too wonderful for the speaker to comprehend.

questions.question: What behavior does Proverbs 30:20 attribute to an adulterous woman?
questions.correctAnswer: She claims innocence
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:20 describes the adulterous woman as one who eats, wipes her mouth, and claims she has done no wickedness, demonstrating denial of her actions.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:21 say causes disquiet in the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: A servant when he reigneth
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:21 states that the earth is disquieted for three things, including when a servant becomes the ruler, indicating a reversal of social order.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:22 say is problematic for the earth?
options: A fool when he is filled with meat
A wise man when he is hungry
A rich man when he is poor
A king when he is humble
questions.correctAnswer: A fool when he is filled with meat
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:22 indicates that a fool being satisfied can lead to unrest and disorder in society.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 30:10 advise regarding accusations against a servant?
options: It is wise to accuse them
It is better to remain silent
It is dangerous to accuse them
questions.correctAnswer: It is dangerous to accuse them
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:10 warns that accusing a servant might result in them cursing you, highlighting the potential repercussions of false accusations.

questions.question: What is one thing Agur asks to be removed from him in Proverbs 30:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Vanity and lies
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:8 shows Agur requesting to be removed from vanity and lies, emphasizing the desire for a truthful life.

questions.question: Is it true that Proverbs 30 emphasizes the importance of humility and acknowledgment of one's limitations?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30 highlights humility, as seen in Agur's admission of his lack of wisdom in verses 2 and 3.

questions.question: Is it false that the earth is disquieted by a wise ruler according to Proverbs 30:21?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:21 states that a servant reigning causes disquiet, not a wise ruler, indicating that leadership matters.

questions.question: Is it false that Proverbs 30 mentions three things that are never satisfied?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:15 notes that there are indeed three things that are never satisfied, but it ultimately concludes with four.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 30 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 30.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 30:25, what characteristic of ants is emphasized despite their small size?
options: They prepare their meat in the summer
They build their houses in the rocks
questions.correctAnswer: They prepare their meat in the summer
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:25 states that ants are not strong but prepare their meat in the summer, highlighting their wisdom in preparation.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 30:27 say about the locusts' leadership?
options: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands
The locusts follow a single leader
The locusts build their nests in the trees
questions.correctAnswer: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:27 explicitly states that locusts have no king yet they move together in groups, emphasizing collective wise behavior without centralized leadership.

questions.question: In Proverbs 30:28, what is unique about the spider's behavior?
options: It taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces
It has a king to lead it
It prepares its food in the summer
questions.correctAnswer: It taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:28 highlights the spider's skill in making webs with its hands and its presence even in the palaces of kings, symbolizing wisdom and subtlety.

questions.question: Which four creatures are described in Proverbs 30:31 as 'comely in going'?
options: A lion, a greyhound, an he goat, and a king
A lion, a horse, a camel, and a king
An eagle, a serpent, a ship, and a man
An ant, a coney, a locust, and a spider
questions.correctAnswer: A lion, a greyhound, an he goat, and a king
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:31 lists these four as comely in their movement: a lion, a greyhound, an he goat, and a king, emphasizing strength, speed, agility, and authority.

questions.question: What advice does Proverbs 30:32 give to someone who has acted foolishly or thought evil?
options: Lay thine hand upon thy mouth
Speak boldly to correct the wrong
questions.correctAnswer: Lay thine hand upon thy mouth
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:32 advises that if one has done foolishly or thought evil, they should restrain themselves by laying their hand upon their mouth, symbolizing silence and self-control.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 30:33, what is produced by the 'forcing of wrath'?
questions.correctAnswer: Strife
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:33 compares the churning of milk producing butter and the wringing of the nose producing blood to the forcing of wrath producing strife, emphasizing the consequences of uncontrolled anger.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'אֱוִיל' ('ewil') in Proverbs 30:2 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Foolish
questions.explanation: In Proverbs 30:2, the Hebrew word 'אֱוִיל' ('ewil') is used to describe Agur as more brutish than any man, meaning 'foolish' or lacking understanding, highlighting humility about wisdom.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Proverbs 30:24-28 to describe the four small but wise creatures?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:24-28 employs parallelism, a Hebrew poetic device, by listing four small creatures and their wise behaviors in a balanced and repetitive structure.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of humility before God as expressed in Proverbs 30:2-3?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 12:3
questions.explanation: Romans 12:3 teaches not to think of oneself more highly than one ought, echoing Proverbs 30:2-3 where Agur acknowledges his lack of wisdom and understanding, highlighting humility.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to Proverbs 30:5 regarding the purity and trustworthiness of God's word?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 12:6
questions.explanation: Psalm 12:6 states that the words of the Lord are pure words, like silver tried in a furnace, connecting directly to Proverbs 30:5's affirmation that every word of God is pure and a shield to trusting believers.

questions.question: What is the verse immediately preceding Proverbs 30:23 which mentions an odious woman when she is married?
options: Proverbs 30:22, For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat
Proverbs 30:21, For three things the earth is disquieted
Proverbs 30:24, There be four things which are little upon the earth
Proverbs 30:20, Such is the way of an adulterous woman
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 30:22, For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:22 immediately precedes verse 23 and is part of the four things the earth cannot bear, connecting contextually with verse 23's listing of further examples.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Proverbs 30:15-16 to describe the 'horseleach' and the unsatisfied things?
questions.correctAnswer: Personification
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:15-16 personifies the horseleach and other elements by describing them as having daughters and expressing insatiable desires, a clear example of personification.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 30:20 use irony to describe the behavior of an adulterous woman?
options: She eats, wipes her mouth, and claims innocence
questions.correctAnswer: She eats, wipes her mouth, and claims innocence
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:20 uses irony as the adulterous woman boldly acts as if she has done no wickedness despite her clear sin, illustrating deceptive confidence.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 30:5 states that every word of God is pure and that He is a shield to those who trust in Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:5 explicitly says, 'Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him,' affirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 30:23 praises the faithful relationship between a handmaid and her mistress.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:23 mentions 'an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress,' indicating a problematic or contentious relationship rather than praise.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 30 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 30 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 30:5 teach about God's nature?
options: God's word is pure and serves as a shield for those who trust in Him
God's wrath is immediate and unrelenting
God's presence is only in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: God's word is pure and serves as a shield for those who trust in Him
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:5 states 'Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.' This highlights the purity and protective nature of God's word for believers.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does Proverbs 30:2 emphasize?
options: Human beings are brutish and lack true understanding apart from divine revelation
Humans are inherently righteous and wise
Sin is only external and does not affect understanding
All men have innate knowledge of holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Human beings are brutish and lack true understanding apart from divine revelation
questions.explanation: In Proverbs 30:2, the speaker confesses, 'Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man,' emphasizing human limitation without God’s wisdom.

questions.question: What doctrine of salvation or sanctification is taught in Proverbs 30:8-9?
options: A balanced life dependent on God prevents denial of God and immoral behavior
Poverty is the only true path to holiness
Self-sufficiency is the goal of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: A balanced life dependent on God prevents denial of God and immoral behavior
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 request God to 'give me neither poverty nor riches,' to avoid denial of God or theft, teaching dependence on God for sanctification and moral integrity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 30:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Proverbs 30:4 questions who has 'ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment?' demonstrating God's omnipotence over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Proverbs 30:6?
options: Holiness in preserving the integrity of His word
Mercy in forgiving additions to scripture
Omniscience in knowing all human thoughts
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness in preserving the integrity of His word
questions.explanation: Verse 6 warns 'Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar,' showing God's holiness in guarding His word's purity.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 30:18-19 prepare for or connect to themes elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It reflects the mystery of God's creation that invites worship and awe
It denies any mystery in God's works
It teaches that all things are fully understandable by human reason
It emphasizes human mastery over nature
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the mystery of God's creation that invites worship and awe
questions.explanation: The 'three things which are too wonderful' in verses 18-19 emphasize the inscrutable ways of God’s creation, preparing themes of divine mystery and awe found in Psalms and Job.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Proverbs 30:20 have with New Testament teachings?
options: It foreshadows the condemnation of unrepentant sinners, similar to warnings in the Epistles
It predicts the literal destruction of adulterous women only
It teaches that sin is always confessed without excuse
It endorses lying about sin as acceptable
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the condemnation of unrepentant sinners, similar to warnings in the Epistles
questions.explanation: Verse 20 describes the adulterous woman denying wickedness, paralleling New Testament admonitions against unrepentant sin (e.g., 1 Corinthians 6:9-10).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 30:7 and 30:8 teach about human dependence on God?
options: That true contentment and sanctification require reliance on God for daily provision and protection from vanity
That human effort alone suffices for wisdom
That God demands riches as proof of favor
That denial of basic needs is the path to holiness
questions.correctAnswer: That true contentment and sanctification require reliance on God for daily provision and protection from vanity
questions.explanation: Verse 7 asks God for two things and verse 8 requests removal of vanity and balanced provision, emphasizing human dependence on God for sanctified contentment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 30:11 and 30:17 teach about the consequences of dishonoring parents?
options: That dishonoring parents leads to divine judgment and loss, emphasizing social and spiritual order
That dishonoring parents has no lasting consequence
That children should be independent from parental authority
That parental curses are always unjust
questions.correctAnswer: That dishonoring parents leads to divine judgment and loss, emphasizing social and spiritual order
questions.explanation: Verse 11 notes a generation cursing their father; verse 17 details the punishment of such disrespect, highlighting consequences for social and divine order.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 30:15 and 30:16 teach about insatiable desires?
options: Certain natural and human conditions symbolize unending desire that only God can satisfy
Desire is always sinful and must be crushed
The grave, womb, earth, and fire are controllable by humans
questions.correctAnswer: Certain natural and human conditions symbolize unending desire that only God can satisfy
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 illustrate 'three things that are never satisfied...four say not, It is enough,' symbolizing insatiable desires reflective of human condition apart from God.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Proverbs 30:6 warns against altering scripture and thus forbids any theological development. What does Proverbs 30:6 actually teach?
options: It warns specifically against adding to God’s revealed word, preserving its purity and authority
It forbids all theological reflection or study
It permits free reinterpretation of scripture without consequence
It teaches that God's word is outdated and should be modernized
questions.correctAnswer: It warns specifically against adding to God’s revealed word, preserving its purity and authority
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states, 'Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee,' emphasizing the importance of preserving scriptural integrity, not forbidding theological development.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 30:24-28 teach about divine providence through creation?
options: God providentially orders even the weakest creatures to act wisely and purposefully
Only humans are under divine providence
Animals act solely by instinct without divine purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially orders even the weakest creatures to act wisely and purposefully
questions.explanation: Verses 24-28 describe small creatures acting wisely despite weakness, illustrating God’s providential care over all creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Proverbs 30:33 with the metaphor of churning milk and wringing the nose?
options: Justice in the consequences of wrath leading to strife
questions.correctAnswer: Justice in the consequences of wrath leading to strife
questions.explanation: Verse 33 uses natural metaphors to show how provoking wrath inevitably produces strife, illustrating God's just ordering of cause and effect.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Proverbs 30:21-23 have with the theme of social order in Scripture?
options: It underscores social unrest caused by role reversals and disruptions of proper authority
It celebrates social upheaval as progress
It denies any importance of social roles
It teaches that servants should always overthrow masters
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores social unrest caused by role reversals and disruptions of proper authority
questions.explanation: Verses 21-23 describe earth’s disquiet over servants reigning and fools filled, linking to biblical emphasis on maintaining divinely ordained social order.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 30:29-31 teach about God’s sovereignty reflected in creation?
options: God’s sovereignty is evident in the strength, dignity, and order of creatures and kings
Creation is chaotic and without order
Kings are always subject to rebellion
Animals and rulers are unrelated to divine sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty is evident in the strength, dignity, and order of creatures and kings
questions.explanation: Verses 29-31 list strong and dignified creatures and a king with no opposition, reflecting God’s sovereign ordering of creation and governance.
